name: Inspection bench: granite surface plate and the inspection instruments
about: One of the shop's workbenches (shop.json benches-1, the support/bench asset) with the height gauge's granite surface plate on it, and the seven inspection instruments where an inspector keeps them: the height gauge and the indicator on the plate, the hand instruments along the bench's front, the gauge-block case at its back. The world frame is the bench asset's, front at -Y and floor at z = 0, so its GLB draws at the origin. Each instrument rests in its own asset frame, underside at z = 0, so its GLB draws at its body's pose; the height gauge and the plate are split out of the hgauge STEP by extract.py (inspection_bench.links.json), the STEP's demonstration part left out.

bench.reason: The bench asset's 72 x 30 in top, 34 in high (bench_top in its placeholder STEP, moved into the asset's frame): a generic bench, no maker's chosen
bench.friction_reason: Steel on a maple top, about 0.4

plate.reason: The shop's own plate (shop.json height-gauge-1, the hgauge record): 12 x 18 x 3 in granite, grade A, a stock size; no maker's chosen
plate.flatness_reason: Grade A at 12 x 18 in: 0.0001 in (GGG-P-463c; ASME B89.3.7)
plate.at_reason: On the bench's left, its long side along the bench, 249 mm of bench in front of it for the part and the hands

contact.reason: Granite and a hard bench top barely give: these sink a resting part well under a micrometre, as a height read off the plate needs. 2 ms is the stiffest stable at the 1 ms timestep

hgauge.boxes_reason: Base, column, slider and scriber, the hgauge STEP's own boxes in the gauge's frame
hgauge.at_reason: Where its STEP stands it on the plate

dti.boxes_reason: The dti asset's bounds: indicator on its magnetic stand
dti.at_reason: On the plate's back left corner, clear of the height gauge, ready to sweep a part on the plate

gblock.boxes_reason: The open case, its lid standing open behind it, and the pin rack: the gblock STEP's own boxes moved into the asset's frame
gblock.at_reason: At the bench's back, out of the way, lid open toward the inspector

cal6.boxes_reason: The cal6 asset's bounds, lying flat
cal6.at_reason: Along the bench's front, right of the plate, in reach

mic1.boxes_reason: The mic1 asset's bounds, lying on its side
mic1.at_reason: Along the bench's front, beside the caliper

thread.boxes_reason: The thread asset's bounds, lying flat
thread.at_reason: Along the bench's front, beside the micrometer

rests_source.reason: Where an inspector keeps each, laid out by its bounds so none touches another or overhangs its surface. Masses are typical for each kind, no maker's figure to hand: a 6 in digital caliper about 0.17 kg, a 0-1 in micrometer 0.2, an indicator on a magnetic stand 1.3 (mostly the stand), an 81-piece block set in its case with pin gauges 3.0, a 12 in digital height gauge 5.0, a portable roughness tester 0.5, a 1/4-20 plug gauge 0.06; each spread through its boxes by volume
